_: THE FIRM'S SETUPS AS ORDINARY DEFINITIONS. TC2000 and TradingView both ship dozens of built-in scans and it is the ONBOARDING PATH, not decoration: a member picks a named setup, gets a WORKING scan, and then EDITS it -- which is how people learn a syntax. A blank formula box loses the wide audience.
_ordinary: EVERY ENTRY IS AN ORDINARY DEFINITION: same store, same `def_hash`, same read-back, editable on arrival. There is no starter flag, no `is_builtin` column and no branch in the save path -- a starter that is special-cased is a second class of object and re-creates the asymmetry spec section 1.1 forbids. This file holds a SOURCE and a frozen TREE; installing one is the member's action through the shipped save path, and the identity is `astHash`'s.
_taxonomy: THE NAMES COME FROM `app/src/constants/setupGroups.js` AND ARE NOT COPIED HERE AS A LIST. This file holds a `source` per setup it can express; the SET of setups and the FAMILY each one belongs to are read from the taxonomy at run time, which is why no entry carries a `family`. A setup with no entry must appear in `_ungrounded` with a reason -- that identity is what makes a NEW setup land RED until somebody decides about it. Two files in this repo carry setup taxonomies and they do not agree: `setupGroups.js` (the labeling taxonomy the Model Book store, the concept vocabulary's attribution check and this file all read) and `app/src/pages/modelbook/setupCatalog.js` (the Setup Library's field-guide, with its own families and its own display names). `setupGroups.js` is authoritative here. Neither count is written down anywhere in this file.
_grounding: GROUNDING IS A LIST OF CITATIONS THAT RESOLVE, AND IT IS RESOLVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED (controller adjudication A-1). Three kinds appear here: `starter_screen` (a screen `saved_screens.py::starters()` ships), `filter_preset` (a labelled threshold in `screener/filters.py::FILTERS`) and `classifier` (a labelled branch of firm code, located by AST). A PLAYBOOK IS NEVER A GROUNDING -- it is prose and cannot mechanically produce a tree -- so the setup name rides as an `attribution`, which this file does not spell either: it is the entry's own KEY.
_no_invented_numbers: EVERY NUMERIC LITERAL IN A STARTER'S TREE MUST BE PUBLISHED BY ONE OF ITS OWN CITATIONS, and every scalar it screens on must be one a citation names. `rs_rank >= 80` is here because the firm ships a preset labelled `Over 80`; 75 would go red NAMING 75. This is the rail that stops a starter from looking like the firm's answer while carrying the catalogue author's opinion.
_no_sentence: NO READ-BACK IS FROZEN HERE, and that is the one place this file deliberately differs from `conceptVocabulary.json`. The card's blurb is `sentenceFor(tree)` in the browser and `sentence_for(tree)` on the server -- derived on every render from the tree that IS the scan. A hand-written blurb would be a second description of one tree and the prose one is the one that drifts (D-A5).
_no_hash: NO `def_hash` IS PRECOMPUTED HERE. The handle is `astHash` over the tree, minted by the shipped save path when a member installs one; a catalogue that carried its own copy would be a second registry and two authorities over one identity.
_ungrounded_rule: A SETUP WITH NO EXPRESSIBLE CONDITION IS NAMED, NOT APPROXIMATED. The member trusts the firm's name on a starter, so a scan that half-means `High Tight Flag` is worse than no scan (AMENDMENT 1's refusal rule, applied to the library). Each reason names its setup and says what is missing -- a column, a published threshold, or the cadence -- because those are three different decisions for the owner. And `rsi(close,14)` is NOT available to close a gap here: E-A9 is open and out of scope, so a setup needing a function the table does not declare stays ungrounded until that phase happens.

_ungrounded.High Tight Flag (Powerplay): High Tight Flag (Powerplay) turns on a PRIOR RUN -- roughly a double in four to eight weeks -- and then a shallow, tight flag on top of it. The table declares `chg_pct_1m` and `pullback_depth_pct`, but the only `chg_pct_1m` preset the screener ships is `Any`, so the size of the run that makes a flag 'high and tight' is still nobody's written-down number -- and the scanner's own run-size column, `pole_pct`, still sits in the closed table's excluded list. Publish a `chg_pct_1m` threshold and this becomes expressible.
_ungrounded.VCP: VCP is the VOLATILITY CONTRACTION pattern, and the contraction SEQUENCE is the tell: successive shallower pullbacks with drying volume into a tight pivot -- the firm's pattern engine, its coach and its course all teach exactly that. The firm DETECTS it -- `screener/patterns.py` emits `vcp` and `FILTERS['pattern']` ships a `VCP` preset -- but the detection lands in `patterns` and `pattern_engine_ids`, comma-joined TEXT lists the closed table excludes by shape, and the pattern scalars the table does declare (`pattern_conf_max`, `pattern_engine_conf`, `pattern_engine_dir`) carry a confidence and a direction with nothing saying WHICH pattern earned them. There is still no `vcp` scalar. The nearest declared boolean, `tight_consolidation`, is a DIFFERENT measurement -- the coefficient of variation of one flat window, no sequence in it -- and the firm's own screen built from it is named `High-RS tight bases`, not VCP. The fix is a per-pattern 0/1 column, not a formula.
_ungrounded.Flat Base Breakout: Flat Base Breakout is a pattern the firm ALREADY DETECTS -- `FILTERS['pattern']` ships a `Flat Base` preset -- but the detection lands in `patterns`, a comma-joined TEXT list the closed table excludes by shape, and there is still no `flat_base` scalar to screen on. `pattern_conf_max` and `pattern_engine_conf` both carry a confidence with nothing attached saying which pattern earned it. The fix is a per-pattern 0/1 column, not a formula.
_ungrounded.IPO Base: IPO Base is defined by how long the symbol has been listed and by WHICH base it is building. The listing-age half is finally in the vocabulary -- `ipo_age_days` is a declared scalar since Wave 2 -- but the only preset the screener ships on it is `Any`, so how young counts as 'recent' is nobody's published number and no citation can ground a threshold. And nothing counts bases: with no `base_count` column anywhere, a first base and a fourth read identically. Publish an `ipo_age_days` preset and the age half grounds in one line.
_ungrounded.Parabolic Short: Parabolic Short is a judgement about the ANGLE of a three-to-five day blow-off and how far it has stretched above its averages. The run half is publishable now -- `consecutive_up` ships a `3+` preset -- but the STRETCH is not: `pct_vs_sma20` ships only `Any`, `pct_vs_ema20` only the `Within 2%` proximity band (the opposite end of the same column), `pct_vs_sma50` and `pct_vs_sma200` carry no filter entry at all, and the scanner's ATR-extension column, `atr_ext_sma50`, sits in the excluded list. The number that makes a move parabolic is still nobody's.
_ungrounded.Parabolic Long: Parabolic Long is the same stretch measurement as Parabolic Short taken from the other side, and it fails the same way: not one `pct_vs_*` column publishes an extension-side threshold, `atr_ext_sma50` is excluded from the closed table, and a nightly row cannot say 'the curve is steepening' without a comparison window nobody has written down -- the offset node could compare today's stretch to last week's, but the week would be this catalogue's number, not the firm's.
_ungrounded.Wedge Pop: Wedge Pop is trendline GEOMETRY -- a converging upper and lower boundary, then a reclaim through the averages. The closed table declares no trendline, no slope and no `wedge` flag; `FILTERS['pattern']` ships six pattern presets and a wedge is not among them; and the pattern engine names its detections only inside `pattern_engine_ids`, a comma-joined list the table permanently excludes. There is nothing to cite.
_ungrounded.Wedge Drop: Wedge Drop is Wedge Pop inverted and stays ungrounded for the mirrored reason: the converging boundaries that define a wedge exist in no column the table declares, in no preset that `FILTERS['pattern']` ships, and in no scalar the pattern engine surfaces -- its names ride `pattern_engine_ids`, a comma-joined list excluded by shape.
_ungrounded.Episodic Pivot: Episodic Pivot is a gap on a MAJOR CATALYST in a neglected name. The gap and the volume are expressible -- `gap_pct` and `vol_ratio` are declared with published thresholds -- and the earnings-dated flavour of the trade already ships as the Power Earnings Gap starter. The catalyst itself is what the table cannot check: it declares no `news` column and no filing column, and a scan called Episodic Pivot that returned every 3% gapper would be putting the firm's name on a guess.
_ungrounded.2B Reversal: 2B Reversal turns on a PRIOR EXTREME being broken and not held, and the offset node that landed in `291c9d8a` finally lets a formula read the bar where the break failed. WHICH extreme is still unsayable: naming it needs `lowest(low, N)` or `highest(high, N)`, and no artifact at the firm publishes an N. The functions exist; the number is still nobody's.
_ungrounded.Kicker Candle: Kicker Candle is a TWO-BAR relationship -- yesterday closes weak, today gaps over yesterday's high and holds it -- and the 8/22 adjudication took it all the way to the last gate: `((close - low) / (high - low))[1] <= 0.33 && open > high[1] && close > high[1]` parses, reads back in the browser lane, is a boolean condition inside budget, and CLEARS THE GROUNDING GATE whole -- 0.33 is `close_position`'s `Bottom third (<0.33)` preset and the citation resolved. What refuses it is the SERVER's read-back: `definition_concierge._render_node` never got the offset branch that `sentence.js::renderOffset` ships (its own canonical-types list names `offset`; the dispatcher refuses it), so `_admit`'s readback gate refuses every offset tree. Port the offset rule and Kicker Candle ships exactly as written.
_ungrounded.News Gappers: News Gappers is the same gap the firm's `Gappers holding gains` starter screen publishes (`gap_pct >= 3 && above_50sma`) -- and, since the flagship presets landed, its bigger cousin `Gap Movers` (`gap_pct >= 8` on 3x volume) -- with one extra claim the table cannot check: that the gap was news-driven. It declares no `news` column, so a member scanning News Gappers would get index rebalances and sympathy moves under a name that promised a catalyst. Ship the screens under their own names, or declare a news column.
_ungrounded.4B Setup (Stan Weinstein): 4B Setup (Stan Weinstein) is a STAGE call -- where the symbol sits in Weinstein's four-stage cycle, read off a 30-week line and its slope. The firm now labels stages: the screener carries `stage2` and `stage4` booleans off the breadth store, with `Weinstein Stage 2` and `Weinstein Stage 4` filters. But both sit in the closed table's excluded list, so there is still no `stage4` scalar a formula can read; the slope booleans beside them (`ema10_rising`, `ema20_rising`) are excluded too, and nothing anywhere measures the 30-week line. Promote the stage booleans and the stage half of this setup grounds in one line.
_ungrounded.Failed H&S/Rounded Top: Failed H&S/Rounded Top is a pattern defined by NOT resolving: everyone sees the top, the breakdown does not come. The offset node (`291c9d8a`) can now read the bars where the breakdown should have printed -- that half of the old objection is gone -- but the NECKLINE is still unnameable: it needs a swing lookback, `lowest(low, N)`, whose N nobody at the firm publishes, and no `neckline` column exists to carry it precomputed.
_ungrounded.Classic U&R: Classic U&R undercuts a PROMINENT PRIOR LOW and reclaims it, and the reclaim -- a two-bar relationship -- is finally sayable through the offset node that landed in `291c9d8a`. The low itself is what remains: `lowest(low, N)` can name a prior low, but which N makes a low prominent is still nobody's published number, and a starter that picked one would be inventing the setup under the firm's name.
_ungrounded.Launchpad: Launchpad's tell is CONVERGENCE, and the closed table still cannot say it. The playbook names the 8-EMA, 21-EMA, 30-SMA and 50-SMA bunched closely together with price consolidating across them, and calls the setup symmetrical: it breaks long or short, and the environment picks the side. The table can now say averages are STACKED -- `ema_stack_intact` is a declared scalar with a `Yes` preset -- but a stacked and widely SEPARATED trend is the opposite of a coiled bundle, and no artifact publishes the band that makes a bundle tight: no `ma_convergence_pct` column, and no published width on any pair of averages. Publish the convergence band and Launchpad becomes expressible.
_ungrounded.Go Signal: Go Signal is a catalyst gap digesting into a short average and then one wide candle closing above the catalyst high. The candle half got closer -- `wide_bar` (>1.5 ATR) is declared with a `Yes` preset, and the offset node can read prior bars -- but the setup still fails twice: the catalyst has no column (the same `news` gap that refuses News Gappers and Episodic Pivot), and the 9-period average Go Signal is defined against is a window no firm artifact publishes. Locating 'the catalyst high' needs the catalyst's date, which is the first gap again.
_ungrounded.HVC: HVC's tell is a LEVEL -- the highest-volume day's close becomes the line the stock must defend -- and the firm already computes the flag: the breadth store tags it, the screener carries it as the `hvc_52w` boolean, and `FILTERS['hvc_52w']` ships it as `High-Volume Close (52W)` with a `Yes` preset. The offset node from `291c9d8a` retired the old two-bar objection as well. One thing is left: the closed table still lists `hvc_52w` among its excluded scalars, so there is no `hvc_52w` scalar a formula can read and no citation that can name it. Promote the column and HVC is a grounded one-liner -- flagged to the controller as exactly that.
_ungrounded.Wick Play: Wick Play is a single-bar discretionary read on where the wick sits relative to the range. `upper_wick_pct` and `lower_wick_pct` ARE declared scalars -- but the only preset the screener ships on either is `Any`, so every threshold this scan could use would be the catalogue author's. Publish a wick preset and Wick Play becomes expressible in one line.
_ungrounded.Slingshot: Slingshot is defined against the 4-period exponential average OF THE HIGHS. `ema` takes any series and `high` is declared, so the shape is within the grammar's reach -- but 4 is not a window any firm artifact publishes, and a starter that picked one would be inventing the setup's own definition. The missing thing is the number, not the grammar.
_ungrounded.Oops Reversal: Oops Reversal gaps BELOW the prior day's low and closes back through it, and the offset node from `291c9d8a` made the whole thing sayable without one invented number: `open < low[1] && close > low[1]` names both bars exactly. What Oops Reversal does not have is a citation -- no starter screen, no preset and no labelled branch of firm code encloses that definition, and the catalogue's rule is that an uncited tree is somebody's opinion rather than the firm's answer. Adjudicated 8/22: the uncited-tree rule is structural (`resolve_grounding` refuses a tree with zero citations, and zero literals waives nothing), so Oops Reversal stays refused until a firm artifact encloses its definition.
_ungrounded.News Failure: News Failure is a headline that does not hold. It needs the headline, and the table declares no `news` column -- the gap that also refuses News Gappers and Episodic Pivot -- and the FAILURE half needs the headline's date besides, to say the move since it has been given back. A nightly snapshot row can check neither half today.
_ungrounded.Remount: Remount requires the symbol to have been BELOW its average and to be back above it, and the 8/22 adjudication closed the old window objection for real: `(close < sma(close, 50))[1] && above_50sma` parses, and the 50 is finally the firm's own number -- a `classifier` citation over `api.services.screener.technicals.compute_technicals`, the branch that writes `above_50sma` off `_sma(closes, 50)`, RESOLVED at the grounding gate, with the `Yes` preset naming the scalar. One refusal is left and it is not the grammar: `definition_concierge` never got the offset branch that `sentence.js` ships, so the readback gate in `_admit` refuses a tree every other walker already proves. Port the offset rule and Remount ships as written.
_ungrounded.Red to Green: Red to Green turns on the zero line -- open below the prior close, close back above it -- and the offset node from `291c9d8a` made that exact sentence legal with no threshold at all: `open < close[1] && close > close[1]`. Two things keep it refused: no firm artifact encloses that definition for a citation to resolve, and the sweep reads the LAST CONFIRMED bar, so a list under this name would show transitions that finished yesterday while the firm trades Red to Green as a live intraday trigger. Adjudicated 8/22: both blockers stand -- zero literals does not waive the citation rule, and the cadence mismatch is the product's honesty line, not a vocabulary gap -- so Red to Green stays refused.
_ungrounded.Opening Range Breakout: Opening Range Breakout is an INTRADAY setup and the sweep is a last-confirmed-DAILY-bar screen. Blocked on cadence (design section 8.5), not on vocabulary: the opening range is not a column the nightly snapshot holds.
_ungrounded.Opening Range Breakdown: Opening Range Breakdown is the short side of the same intraday range and is blocked on the same cadence: the sweep runs on the last confirmed daily bar and the snapshot carries no opening range.
_ungrounded.Red to Green (Intraday): Red to Green (Intraday) is explicitly intraday and the sweep is a last-confirmed-DAILY-bar screen. Blocked on cadence (design section 8.5).
_ungrounded.Green to Red: Green to Red is the intraday mirror of Red to Green (Intraday) and is blocked on the same cadence: nothing in a daily snapshot can name a session crossing its own opening reference.
_ungrounded.30min Pivot: 30min Pivot is defined against the first half-hour's high, which exists only on an intraday timeframe. Blocked on cadence (design section 8.5).
_ungrounded.Mean Reversion L/S: Mean Reversion L/S is an INTRADAY setup, and the sweep is a last-confirmed-DAILY-bar screen. Blocked on design section 8.5 (cadence), not on vocabulary.
